uncited: In full pre-integration, the color contribution $C$ along a ray segment is computed by integrating the product of the emitted color and the accumulated opacity (attenuation).
This error is most noticeable when opacity is high, as the lack of attenuation leads to over-brightening of colors behind dense regions.

Both sources confirm that neglecting attenuation is the mechanism used to achieve faster performance (solving the bottleneck) compared to full pre-integration.
